name: Boulogne-sur-Mer
title: Boulogne-sur-Mer Trawler Thickness Measurement | UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Boulogne-sur-Mer, France's leading fishing port: trawlers, reefer carriers, dredgers and cargo ships, hull and tank gauging.
h1: Fishing Vessel and Cargo Ship Gauging at Boulogne-sur-Mer
intro: Boulogne-sur-Mer is France's leading fishing port, with a trawler fleet, a large seafood processing district and commercial quays that take reefers, aggregates and dredgers. Fishing vessels and workboats here are worked hard, and owners, buyers and insurers want measured steel before repairs and sales. A team mobilised from India to Boulogne gauges vessels at the fish quays, the repair berths and the cargo quays on the River Liane.

highlights.p: Trawlers of many sizes work out of Boulogne, and their hulls, fish holds and fuel tanks wear in a corrosive, abrasive trade. Between trips they are in port long enough for focused gauging, planned with the skipper.

Refrigerated cargo ships and ro-ro units serve the processing district beside the harbour. Their calls follow the market, and a short stay at the quay can suit deck, hatch and tank gauging agreed with the agent.

Sand and aggregate ships, dredgers and service craft use the commercial berths. Their piping, hopper plating and hull structure suffer abrasion, and measured readings between campaigns show where repairs are needed first.

port.h: Boulogne-sur-Mer: a Channel fishing port on the River Liane estuary
p: Boulogne-sur-Mer stands at the mouth of the River Liane on the Côte d'Opale, a short run south of Calais. The commercial port, the fish quays and the marina are protected by long breakwaters, and the harbour is run by the same operating company as Calais, under the Port Boulogne-Calais banner for the Hauts-de-France region. The Channel tide is large here, and the available depth in the basins and along the river quays changes through the day, so movements are planned around the water and pilots are widely used.

Fishing defines the port. Boulogne's fleet includes otter trawlers, beam trawlers, netters and smaller coastal boats, and landings feed a fish market and a processing district beside the harbour that is among the largest seafood centres in Europe. Alongside the fleet, the commercial berths take refrigerated ships and ro-ro units for the processing trade, sand and aggregate carriers, general cargo ships and dredgers. Tugs, pilot boats, rescue craft and a good number of workboats support the port, and the Strait's dense shipping lanes lie just offshore.

The fishing calendar controls availability. Boats leave and return to a pattern set by species, quota and weather, and many come back to port for a few days between trips, with longer stays during repairs or closed seasons. Winter gales and rough sea on the Channel often keep the fleet alongside, which creates windows for gauging. The commercial side runs to the market's rhythm, with reefers and aggregate ships on regular calls, and a team that plans around both can usually find a suitable slot for most vessel types.

facilities.h: Where vessels can be gauged at Boulogne-sur-Mer
p: The fish quays are the main working area. A trawler alongside between trips is generally clean and available, and the skipper can release fish holds, fuel and ballast tanks, and deck areas for gauging once the crew have ventilated them. Fishing vessels often carry modifications that do not match their original drawings, so we record the layout found on board and gauge to the owner's drawings where they exist. Repair berths and boatyards along the Liane handle fishing vessels and workboats, and readings taken beforehand help owners and yards fix the scope of the work.

The commercial quays suit larger and longer stays. Reefers and ro-ro units discharge to the processing district on a regular cycle, aggregate carriers and dredgers lie for loading or discharge, and general cargo ships come and go. Ships needing a full drydocking at deeper yards usually go to another port, and a gauging programme at Boulogne can be timed to produce the steel estimate before that decision. Anchorage outside the breakwaters is available for ships waiting for tide or berth, when sea state permits a launch.
list: Fish quays — fish hold, tank and deck gauging on trawlers and netters between trips.
Repair berths and boatyards on the Liane — hull and tank gauging before and during repair work on fishing vessels and workboats.
Commercial quays — hatch cover, deck and tank gauging on reefers, ro-ro units and general cargo ships during cargo gaps.
Aggregate and dredger berths — pump, discharge piping and hopper plating gauging between campaigns.
Lay-by berths — extended condition gauging for pre-purchase or insurer surveys on vessels laid up.
Roads outside the breakwaters — launch-assisted gauging of cleaned tanks on waiting ships in suitable weather.

context.h: French fishing vessel rules, port state control and the Strait
p: Port state control in France is exercised by the Centres de sécurité des navires of the Affaires maritimes administration, within the Paris MoU, and applies to foreign cargo ships calling at Boulogne. French-flag fishing vessels fall under national safety rules and are surveyed by the Affaires maritimes, with many boats unclassed. A gauging report is therefore usually requested by an owner, a buyer, a bank or an insurer and can be shown to the surveyor if asked, while classed vessels follow their society's reading format and extent.

Boulogne lies in the SECA part of the Channel, so ships that carry scrubbers use them on nearly every voyage. EU ship recycling rules require an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships above the size threshold, and the EU emissions trading scheme and FuelEU Maritime apply to the larger ships calling here. For owners of older trawlers and coasters, measured wastage is the evidence used to decide between a major refit, replacement and sale, and a thickness report is a straightforward way to put that decision on firm ground.

jobs.p: Most jobs here begin with a phone call from an owner or a superintendent who has a repair, a sale or an insurance renewal coming up. We agree a scope against the vessel's drawings, plan around the tide and the fishing calendar, and send a small team sized to the work. The report is arranged by tank or area so that the yard, the buyer or the insurer can use it directly, and for classed vessels it follows the society's format.
list: Fish hold, fuel and ballast tank gauging on a trawler between trips, ahead of a yard repair.
Hull and deck gauging on a second-hand fishing vessel for a buyer or a bank.
Hatch cover, deck and tank gauging on a reefer ship discharging for the processing district.
Pump, suction and discharge piping gauging on a dredger between campaigns.
Intermediate survey preparation on a coastal cargo ship alongside the commercial quay.

logistics: Paris Charles de Gaulle and Brussels are the usual arrival airports, followed by train or road to Boulogne, with Lille Lesquin as a regional option. Technicians travel from India on Schengen visas applied for once the vessel's dates are firm, supported by an invitation letter from the owner or manager. Quay access and any work in the processing district's secure areas is arranged through the ship's agent or the vessel owner, and plans allow for tide, weather and the fishing schedule.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a fishing vessel's fish holds and tanks at Boulogne?
faqs.a: Yes, once the spaces are cleaned, ventilated and certified safe by the crew. Fish holds and tanks corrode at welds, stiffeners and the tank top, and we measure those details first. The report is arranged by space, and where the boat's layout differs from its drawings we record what is found on board.

faqs.q: Is thickness measurement useful for unclassed fishing boats?
faqs.a: Yes. Without class rules, owners, buyers, banks and insurers rely on independent evidence of steel condition. A gauging report shows measured plate thickness against the original and where wastage is concentrated, which helps in negotiating a sale, planning repairs or supporting an insurance renewal.

faqs.q: Can the work be done during a short stay between trips?
faqs.a: A focused scope can. A few days between trips is enough for hold, fuel tank and deck gauging if the crew prepare the spaces in advance. We agree the priority areas with the skipper, start with those, and report what was reached so the owner can plan the remainder for a longer stay.

faqs.q: Where do larger ships go for a docking if they call at Boulogne?
faqs.a: Larger ships generally dock at a bigger yard in another port, and the gauging done at Boulogne feeds the steel estimate for that yard. One Schengen visa covers a trip that includes Boulogne, Calais, Dunkirk or a Belgian port, so a combined plan is often possible if the owner has several ships in the region.
